The text contrasts two perspectives on human nature. William Golding’s *Lord of the Flies* presents the theme of inherent evil, suggesting that humans are naturally savage and descend into barbarism when removed from societal constraints. In contrast, Jean-Jacques Rousseau’s philosophy posits that humans are naturally good and free, and it is society that corrupts them. The similarity lies in both texts addressing the fundamental nature of humanity and the role of civilization. The difference lies in their conclusions: Golding argues that evil is innate, while Rousseau argues that goodness is innate and society is the corrupting influence.

The organ that pumps blood is the heart.
